title: Tie-Breaking Independence: Validating Cross-Model Disagreement as an Uncertainty Signal

original_idea.body:
# Tie-Breaking Independence: Validating Cross-Model Disagreement as an Uncertainty Signal

**Problem:** Success state: a deployed system can safely escalate to a human exactly when models disagree, trusting that agreement implies correctness.

**Direction:** On labeled safety/QA tasks, collect per-item agreement across several open models and measure calibration: does higher cross-model agreement actually predict higher accuracy?

**Why it matters:** Disagreement-triggered human review is a leading cheap safety pattern. If homogeneity makes models unanimously and confidently wrong, the escalation system stays silent exactly when it should fire.

**Relevant context:** Synthesizes correlated-error findings with Artificial Hivemind homogeneity.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: validating agreement-as-confidence directly affects whether disagreement-triggered human escalation is trustworthy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Labeled QA sets + agreement/accuracy calibration plots; accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: accuracy-vs-agreement calibration with clear deliverable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public-model eval of a cheap safety heuristic, independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference over labeled sets, single GPU, no training.

novelty.reasoning: Agreement-accuracy calibration partly studied; the homogeneity-breaks-escalation framing may be open.
